What happens, in order, and why
1 The customer builds the move in the calculator: items and weights, addresses with any stops, and an available date.
2 The calculator estimates the price from the price list and the distance over all the legs. The customer submits it.
3 The web quote reaches the sales person as a request. A second request from the same contact is flagged.
4 The sales person calls the booker to go through the move, and fixes anything missing or wrong.
5 The customer says yes. If the date turned out to be full, the sales person asks the manager for an exception.
6 The sales person takes the deposit through the payment provider.
7 The deposit is recorded in the customer account. If the card is declined, there is no move yet.
8 With the deposit in, the sales person creates the move: the price is locked and the date is set.
9 The move appears on the schedule.
10 The manager and the crew both see it.
11 The manager assigns the move to a crew, with its trucks, in the day plan.
12 On the day the foreman records what happens: set off, arrived, waited, extras, damage, done, or an extra day.
13 The balance falls due and is paid. The sales person's share comes only from money received.
• A web quote is only a request, and there is one open request per move.
• No move without a deposit: the yes is recorded first, and the move is
created once the deposit is in.
• A confirmed move changes only through a change request, re-priced
from the price list and accepted again.
• Cancelling within 7 days of the move keeps the deposit.
• Only the manager assigns crews, accepts a full date and adds a day.
• A move can have several stops and more than one day; it is still one move.
• The foreman records the day; a move that didn't happen is recorded
by the manager, with the reason and whose fault it was.
